new_bank_questions.title: Equal moments with changing laws
new_bank_questions.body: Let independent $X_t$ be $-1$ or $1$ equally likely at even times, and let it be $0$ with probability $1/2$ and each of $-\sqrt2,\sqrt2$ with probability $1/4$ at odd times. Compute the mean, variance and nonzero-lag covariance. Is the process weakly stationary? Is it strictly stationary? Explain.
new_bank_questions.answer: At either parity the mean is $0$. The even-time variance is $1$; the odd-time variance is $(1/4)2+(1/4)2=1$. Independence makes covariance $0$ at every nonzero lag. Thus the mean and lag covariance are time invariant and the process is weakly stationary. Its one-time law alternates between a two-point and a three-point distribution, so it is not strictly stationary.
